text:
alex: FYI—AcmeCorp pinged support. They see a spike of streaming requests being marked 5xx, but the client claims they closed the connection. They're also disputing billing because token counts show full output billed even when client hung up early. Attach: sample logs + curl repro.

jamie: Can you paste the exact gateway/proxy error lines and the request-id? Need to correlate with telemetry. :eyes:

alex: request-id=rc-20231115-7f3a, log excerpt:``` 
[2023-11-15T14:12:02.123Z] proxy=gw-17 write to backend failed: write tcp 10.0.4.23:443->10.0.8.101:54932: broken pipe (EPIPE)
[2023-11-15T14:12:02.123Z] gateway=gw-17 upstream status=502 path=/v1/stream generate request_id=rc-20231115-7f3a
[2023-11-15T14:12:02.124Z] billing=metering token_count=1189 request_id=rc-20231115-7f3a
```
They also sent a curl-based repro:```bash
# client opens stream then closes after 1s
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  --data-binary $'4\r\nTest\r\n0\r\n' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream --max-time 2
```
It reproduces EPIPE on our side.

nora: Quick context: our metric pipeline currently marks a request as 5xx when the gateway sees an upstream write failure or non-2xx upstream status. Historically that lumps together server faults and client-side aborts (e.g., client sent RST/FIN). We do have an abort-detection heuristic but it misses a few proxy-edge races (half-close vs full RST).

nora: From the logs it looks like the proxy attempted to flush bytes after the client half-closed. If the client sent a FIN, kernel returns EPIPE on write — that should be a client abort (non-5xx) for both reliability and billing. But if upstream returned a 5xx before the client closed, it's a server error. We need a better distinguishing signal (SO_ERROR / socket shutdown direction) in gateway traces.

maya: Holding billing on this request_id until we triage. Please add the full token-meter details and RAW request body so I can verify billed tokens vs produced tokens.

alex: token meter excerpt included above but here's the raw meter snapshot:```
request_id: rc-20231115-7f3a
produced_tokens: 402
billed_tokens: 1189
client_disconnect_ts: 2023-11-15T14:12:02.080Z
gateway_error_ts: 2023-11-15T14:12:02.123Z
```
Customer insists produced_tokens << billed_tokens.

cj: I told AcmeCorp we've opened an investigation and put a billing hold. They're anxious — can we get an ETA?

jamie: Next steps I'm proposing: (1) Enable socket-level debug on gw-17 to capture tcp FIN/RST direction for ~1 hour, (2) get pcap on gw-17 for the timeframe, (3) run the curl repro with our test client and collect kernel socket states.

repro-bot: Minimal repro that forces early client close:```bash
# server: stream long output every 200ms
# client: close after N chunks
( for i in {1..100}; do printf "%s\n" "chunk-$i"; sleep 0.2; done ) | nc -l 8000 &
sleep 1; printf "GET /stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n0\r\n" | nc localhost 8000; # then kill client socket
```
This reliably creates EPIPE on server write in our env.

nora: Thanks — I reproduced locally. Observed sequence: client FIN -> server write -> errno EPIPE -> our gateway code logs upstream write failed -> we mark 5xx. Bug: we call mark_5xx() before checking whether the peer initiated shutdown. I can prepare a patch to check for socket shutdown (MSG_NOSIGNAL or SO_ERROR readback) and flag as client_abort.

jamie: If that's the fix, we should ship a rollback-safe change: add feature-flag guarded check, run canary for 12 hours. Also add a metric that counts EPIPE separated by peer-initiated vs server-timed-out.

maya: Billing ask: if patch lands, do we retroactively credit affected requests from the window where behavior misclassified? We need numbers. Can infra produce list of request_ids where produced_tokens < billed_tokens and gateway logged EPIPE?

nora: Yes, I can add a query: select request_id where gateway_error='EPIPE' and produced_tokens < billed_tokens. I'll run it after we enable debug. Estimate ~200 requests in last 24h (wild guess).

alex: Action items summarized:
- [nora] prepare patch to treat peer-initiated socket closure as client_abort, feature-flag it (ETA: 1d).
- [jamie] enable socket debug + pcap on gw-17 for 1h, collect captures (ETA: 2h).
- [alex] collect full request/response bodies for rc-20231115-7f3a and attach to ticket (in progress).
- [maya] place billing hold on suspect requests and draft customer-facing note (done).
- [cj] let customer know we prioritized and will follow up within 24h.

maya: Thanks all. Holding billing and emailed AcmeCorp with: "We've placed a temporary credit hold while we investigate a possible misclassification of client disconnects that may have caused overbilling." :white_check_mark:

jamie: :thumbsup: once we have pcap/nora's patch we can decide whether credits need to be applied retroactively.

alex: I'll post back here with the pcap + kernel socket dump when available. For now, reassigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

nora: Will open a PR with tests that simulate client FIN during mid-stream and validate we do not mark 5xx / do not bill extra tokens.

alex: Great. Closing loop: this thread will be updated with PR link + billing query results.

cj: Thanks — customer appreciated the quick response. :pray:
